newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mixed in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mixed in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mixed Wednesday in thin pre-holiday trading in tandem with physical prices in the western U.S.

Spot cash prices in the Pacific Northwest were pressured by seasonal temperatures, while those in the Southwest were supported by colder-than-normal weather in eastern Arizona and New Mexico for the rest of the week, brokers and traders.

In the western wholesale power market, January values for delivery at the California-Oregon Border (COB) finished at $25.25-$25.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), flat from Tuesday. January physical prices at the Palo Verde (PV) switchyard in Arizona were ended at $25.50-$26.50, up from Tuesday's $24.00-$25.00.
January 1997 COB futures settled at $25.67, down 51 cents a megawatt hour (MWh) after traded between $25.30 and $26.25.
February 1997 COB finished down 40 cents at $20.10. The rest of the COB contracts were inactive.
January 1997 PV futures settled up 51 cents at $25.35 after bouncing between a 40 cent range.
Most brokers and traders said the higher settlement of January PV stemmed from short-covering by a few players before the long holiday weekend.
February 1997 PV finished down 50 cents at $21.00 and March 1997 PV ended 30 cents at $19.70. Other deferred PV months were quiet.
NYMEX estimated 42 COB and 16 PV contracts changed hands.
A 550 megawatt (MW) coal-fired unit at the Laramie River generating station in Wheatland, Wyo., will shut today for planned maintenance and will restart Sunday.

The 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear unit in Avila Beach, Calif., was still expected to resume operation by Friday after being off line last Friday following a fire in an auxiliary power grounding transformer.
The 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear generating complex in San Clemente, Calif., began ramping down ahead of a 70-day refueling outage which was planned to start Saturday.
The New York Mercantile Exchange and most West utilities will be closed Thursday and Friday in observance of the Thanksgiving holiday weekend.
